title: Built a VHS rental store tycoon game solo with AI-assisted development — demo just went live on itch.io
author: GoatNo466
selftext:
Hey r/aigamedev,  
I wanted to share the release of the demo for my game, VHS Store Tycoon—a pixel-art tycoon game set in an ’80s/’90s video store, built in Godot 4.6.2.  
About the development process:  
I worked with a fairly specific AI-assisted development workflow, with line-by-line code review before each implementation. The rule that helped me the most: never accept an implementation just based on the text summary provided by the AI—always verify it directly in the actual code. It saved me from several subtle bugs that the summary said were “fixed” but in practice weren’t.  
About the game:  
  
Buy movie rights, organize shelves, hire employees (cashiers, cleaners, “rewinders”)  
Dynamic competition system: rival stores that attack your business based on your capital  
Over 320 parody movies with custom descriptions  
Localized into 8 languages  
The demo covers the first 11 days of gameplay  
  
Link to the demo (free): [Jugar Demo VHS Store Tycoon ](https://lofidevs.itch.io/vhs-store-tycoon)  
If you’re curious about the workflow or the verification process I used, I’d be happy to answer questions in the comments.

comments.author: Cry_Havoc_1990
comments.body:
How did you get the pixel art? Did you design it yourself? 

I’ve been trying to lock in the pixel art aesthetic but generating sprite sheets blocks me heavily

replies.author: GoatNo466
replies.body:
Hi!👋 

Of course, what I did was take a sprite sheet from Google and upload it to Gemini. I know it’s not the best agent for creating pixel art, but it didn’t do too badly; I had to give it some additional instructions to fix it, but it still did a decent job. I need to improve it, of course, but if it worked for me, I’m sure it’ll work for you too. So I sent Gemini the sprite sheet and told it, “I need you to carefully and thoroughly analyze this image and tell me everything it contains.” Once it responds with all the details, based on that I send it an image of a character it can use for inspiration—without making it an exact copy due to copyright issues—and I tell it that, taking into account the sprite sheet I’ve provided, it should generate an image of this character while maintaining the animations from the sprite sheet… Generally speaking, that’s what I did. Afterward, I ran into some issues because it turns out they send you an image with very high resolution and quality, and in a pixel art game you have to control the resolution: they need to be 16x16, 32x32, or 128x128, so that was my challenge—I had to use tools to resize the images and remove the backgrounds… but that’s more or less the gist of what I did; I hope it helps you. See you later! ✌️
